findings.title: Codec v1-only message compatibility change has no test
findings.why_it_matters: The stated intent is to keep working for users whose messages are v1-only generated types. The codec now asserts `v.(proto.Message)` against google.golang.org/protobuf/proto.Message (requires ProtoReflect), so a v1-only message that implemented the old golang/protobuf Message (Reset/String/ProtoMessage) now fails with 'message is %T, want proto.Message'. The only codec tests (TestBasicProtoCodecMarshalAndUnmarshal, TestConcurrentUsage, benchmarks) use the v2-generated pb.Buffer, so nothing detects this regression or proves the compatibility claim. Adding a test with a v1-only message type (and fixing the codec to wrap via protoadapt.MessageV2Of/protoimpl.X.ProtoMessageV2Of) would pin the contract.
findings.suggested_fix: In encoding/proto/proto_test.go add a table case that marshals/unmarshals a hand-written v1-only message (struct with Reset/String/ProtoMessage and protobuf struct tags) through codec{}, and have the codec fall back to protoadapt.MessageV2Of for non-v2 messages. Assumption: v1-only support is meant to be preserved for the codec as the intent states.
evidence: encoding/proto/proto.go:42 -- vv, ok := v.(proto.Message)   (proto is now google.golang.org/protobuf/proto)
encoding/proto/proto_test.go:31-36 -- p := &pb.Buffer{}; marshalledBytes, err := codec.Marshal(p)  (v2-generated type only)

findings.title: Invalid load_reporting_interval error path untested and logs <nil> cause
findings.why_it_matters: The rewritten branch checks `rInterval.CheckValid() != nil` but formats the unrelated `err` variable (which is nil after a successful stream.Recv()), so a bad or missing load_reporting_interval from the management server yields 'invalid load_reporting_interval: <nil>' with no reason. The only test in this package (TestReportLoad) sends a valid 50ms interval, so the changed error path is never exercised and the lost diagnostic was not caught.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture the error: `if err := rInterval.CheckValid(); err != nil { return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("invalid load_reporting_interval: %v", err) }`, and add a transport/loadreport_test.go case where the first LoadStatsResponse has a nil or out-of-range LoadReportingInterval and assert ReportLoad's error text contains the validation reason.
evidence: xds/internal/xdsclient/transport/loadreport.go:174-175 -- if rInterval.CheckValid() != nil {\n return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("invalid load_reporting_interval: %v", err)
xds/internal/xdsclient/transport/loadreport_test.go:94 -- LoadReportingInterval: &durationpb.Duration{Nanos: 50000000}, // 50ms (only interval value used in tests)

residual_risks: internal/pretty has no test file; ToJSON's v1 branch moved from jsonpb to protojson.MarshalOptions{Indent} (and protov1.MessageV2 conversion), changing formatting/failure behavior for v1 messages with no test pinning it (logging only, so low impact).

Most of the diff (about 60 files) is import swaps in tests; I did not run the suite, so compile/behavior of the rewritten tests (e.g. status_test Details comparison via protoreflect.ProtoMessage assertion, protoimpl.X.NewError expected error string) was verified only by reading.
testing_gaps: No test exercises Status.WithDetails/Details with a v1-only message (non-ProtoReflect type) even though WithDetails now takes protoadapt.MessageV1 specifically to support them; status_test and handler_server_test use v2-generated errdetails types only.
